text.p: Zmax Corp said Tuesday it filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission a proposed recapitalization of the company.
Zmax, which is based in Germantown, Md., operates Century Services Inc, which has developed "Vision 2000," a system for correcting computer code dates that terminate in the year 2000.

In the filing, Zmax said the recapitalization involves an exchange offer of the company's 8.0 subordinated debentures for common stock and warrants, the exercise of warrants issued to debentures holders in the exchange offer and reincorporation of the company under Delaware law.
After the SEC approves the registration, the exchange offer will be made, it said.
Each debenture holder will be offered 220 common shares and a warrant to buy 220 common shares for each $1,000 principal amount of debentures exchanged.
The warrants are immediately exercisable upon issuance, at $7 a share, increasing to $8 a share on the first anniversary of their issuance and expires on the second anniversary.

The exchange offer and the reincorporation can go through only if holders of warrants representing at least 80 percent of the common shares issuable agree to immediately exercise their warrants, it said.
